title: Sunset multiplexed long-polling/batch endpoints and migrate clients to unified responses API (PRD)
creator: Priya Nambiar
summary: Decommission the legacy multiplexed long-polling and batch endpoints used by older SDKs and internal integrations. Replace with the unified Responses API (responses-v2) and provide a compatibility adapter, clear migration guidance, and a phased sunset timeline to minimize client disruptions.
background: Over the last 18 months we introduced several transport variants for serving inference (long-polling multiplexed endpoints, a batched-polling interface used by desktop clients, and the streaming SSE-based chat endpoints). These created maintenance overhead, inconsistent semantics (partial messages, differing retry/backoff behaviors), and billing discrepancies. Responses-v2 consolidates streaming, structured outputs, and batch multiplexing into a single contract that supports server-side routing, per-request token billing, and robust reconnect semantics. Maintaining the older multiplexed long-polling and batch endpoints prevents simplification of the runtime, increases operational surface area, and slows feature rollout across Dedicated and Private deployments.
goals: 1) Provide a safe, well-documented migration path from legacy multiplexed long-polling and batch endpoints to responses-v2. 2) Ship a compatibility adapter in our SDKs to reduce immediate client breakage. 3) Retire legacy endpoints after a staged ramp-down with monitoring and rollback capability. 4) Ensure parity for observability, billing, and function-calling semantics in responses-v2.
success_metrics:
- 90% of production traffic on hosted API should use responses-v2 or SDK compatibility adapter within 90 days of adapter release.
- <5% of requests to legacy endpoints after 120 days from adapter release.
- No critical production incidents caused by migrations (P0 incidents).
- Migration guide rated >=4/5 by early adopter customers in feedback survey.
scope_in:
- Legacy multiplexed long-polling endpoints (e.g., /v1/legacy/multiplex/poll).
- Batched poll endpoints used by desktop clients (e.g., /v1/batch/poll).
- SDK compatibility adapter implementation for JavaScript and Python.
- Migration documentation, sample conversion scripts, and client checklists.
- Billing transition mapping and telemetry updates to Console.
scope_out:
- Deprecation of chatstream SSE endpoints (handled in separate initiative).
- On-prem runtime agents' upgrade mechanism beyond providing the migration spec (Operations will coordinate separately).
- Third-party proxies that implement custom client-side multiplexing (we will provide guidance but not validation).
migration_strategy:
Phased approach: 1) Adapter & docs (6 weeks): ship SDK compatibility adapters that translate legacy multiplexed requests to responses-v2 semantics, including retry/backoff and reconnect behavior. 2) Early adopter program (4 weeks): invite largest affected customers to test adapters and provide migration feedback. 3) Opt-in migration window (60 days): enable responses-v2 by default for new keys and offer an opt-in toggle for existing keys; keep legacy endpoints available but throttled to discourage new usage. 4) Forced deprecation notice (30 days): mark legacy endpoints read-only with explanatory 299/notification headers and dashboard banners; continue telemetry. 5) Sunset: after communications and remediation window, return 410 for legacy endpoints and remove support.
All phases will include targeted email and Console banners and a dedicated migration FAQ.
timeline:
- 2026-02-16: Kickoff and requirement signoff.
- 2026-03-01: Public PRD and roadmap published.
- 2026-03-22: SDK compatibility adapters shipped (JS + Python) + migration docs.
- 2026-04-05: Early adopter cohort onboarded.
- 2026-04-21: Open opt-in migration begins; new keys default to responses-v2.
- 2026-06-01: Start forced deprecation notices and console warnings.
- 2026-06-30: Legacy endpoints return 410s (sunset complete).
acceptance_criteria:
- Compatibility adapters for JS and Python exist in our public SDKs and have automated test suites.
- A migration guide and checklist published in Console docs with code examples for common patterns (multiplexed streams, batch poll, reconnects, function calls).
- Billing mapping validated: token accounting for adapter-translated requests matches legacy billing for a representative sample.
- Telemetry dashboards showing endpoint usage, error surface, and migration progress are created and published to product + support.
- Support runbook and escalation path documented; on-call notified of migration windows.
- Legal and Security reviewed the adapter behavior and documentation (security_review_required=true).
rollout_plan:
- Week 0 (adapter release): feature flags off; make adapter available in SDKs; internal teams migrate test workloads.
- Week 2: Public docs and migration checklist; communicate to top 40 customers; create migration support Slack channel.
- Week 6: Enable opt-in default for new keys; monitor metrics.
- Week 10-14: Communications ramp (emails, console banners, changelog).
- Week 15: Begin forced deprecation warning; enable 299 notification headers for legacy endpoints.
- Week 20: Sunset enforced (410).
Rollback: re-enable legacy endpoints and pause sunset if >3 significant regressions within a 7-day window.
client_sdk_changes:
- JS SDK: 'legacyMultiplexAdapter' module that maps legacy multiplex frames to responses-v2 streaming events; provide polyfill for token billing headers and reconnect semantics.
- Python SDK: 'LegacyMultiplexCompat' class with the same interface as legacy client to minimize code changes.
- New samples: migration-playbook-js.md and migration-playbook-py.md.
- Deprecation warnings surfaced at runtime via console.warn() and telemetry tags for server-side clients.
- Backwards compatibility: adapter will support older authentication tokens but will log a migration hint header.
monitoring_and_success_metrics_details:
- Dashboards: legacy-endpoint-volume, adapter-conversion-errors, adapter-latency-p50/p90, billing-discrepancy-rate.
- Alerts: >1% adapter-conversion-error-rate sustained for 30 minutes; >10% drop in throughput for responses-v2 after adapter rollout.
- Data retention: migration metrics retained for 90 days for postmortem analysis.
- Customer-facing status: Console migration progress widget with percent migrated and top failing customers.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Adapter changes semantics subtly (ordering/retry) causing unseen regressions. Mitigation: extensive integration tests that replay recorded production traffic and cross-validate outputs.
- Risk: High-volume customers may rely on batching semantics that are not 1:1. Mitigation: dedicated migration engineering sprints with top 10 customers.
- Risk: Billing mismatch due to tokenization differences. Mitigation: run side-by-side billing reconciliation for the first 30 days and offer credits for verified mismatches.
- Risk: Slow adoption leading to prolonged support burden. Mitigation: incentivize migration via new-key defaults, deprecation timelines, and personalized migration assistance.
notes:
- Coordinate timing with Dedicated & Private release windows to ensure on-prem customers have upgrade paths.
- Plan a customer webinar during the opt-in migration window to walk through common conversions (multiplex frames -> responses events).
- Track top 20 customers still using legacy endpoints weekly and assign a named PM/SE to each.
review_feedback:
- Design: ensure streaming UX in responses-v2 covers partial artifacts (DESIGN-334).
- Security: require client-side adapter to avoid storing unencrypted logs and to propagate KMS headers.
- SRE: prefer 30-day opt-in window if adapter telemetry shows >0.5% error rate during early adopter phase.
